name: The James Kinzie household
head: kinzie_james

arrival.note: A BOUND BECOMES A YEAR, ON A CARD THAT SAID IN TERMS THAT NOTHING DATED IT. Moses and Kirkland, History of Chicago vol. 1 (1895), printed pages 78-79, the table headed LIST OF ACTUAL SETTLERS AT CHICAGO, PRIOR TO 1830 (data/research/books/records/moses_kirkland_v1_actual_settlers_pre_1830.json). It is an 1895 compilation crediting Hurlbut's Chicago Antiquities pp. 37-8 three lines above itself, every row transcription_mediated and none scan_verified, so NOTHING READ OFF IT IS GRADED ABOVE `inferred` HERE. Row bk_mose1_as_018 reads 'Kinzie, James', nativity Detroit, YEAR 1824, remarks 'Voted in 1830, born April 21, 1793, died Jan. 3, 1868'; the table separates the three Kinzies itself and this row carries a full forename rather than an initial, which is what the books crosswalk merged it on. WHAT THIS RECORD USED TO SAY: "He is in the settlement by 1831, when he stands surety on the ferry bond. Nothing dates his coming." — 1831 was the ferry bond, a LATEST-BY and not a coming, and the record admitted it. The table's 1824 is a coming, it is seven years earlier, and it is consistent with the bond: a man in the settlement by 1824 is in it by 1831. INFERRED AND NOT ATTESTED: 1895, at second hand from Hurlbut, transcription_mediated. WHAT DOES NOT FOLLOW: the table's own preamble bounds it BEFORE 1830 and its remarks are civic acts of 1825-1830. A man on it is not thereby at Chicago on 1835-07-01, and this edit moves no residence, no `present_on_scene_date` and no grade. The identity is the books crosswalk's landed merge (T-0961) and is not re-opened here.

origin.note: A DRAWN REGION IS REPLACED BY A PRINTED NATIVITY. It is an 1895 compilation crediting Hurlbut's Chicago Antiquities pp. 37-8 three lines above itself, every row transcription_mediated and none scan_verified, so NOTHING READ OFF IT IS GRADED ABOVE `inferred` HERE. prints his nativity as Detroit. IT IS ALSO THE PLACE THE FAMILY IS ALREADY ATTACHED TO in this layer — the card holds him half-brother to John Harris Kinzie — so the cell agrees with what the town already knows about the household rather than standing alone. A man on it is not thereby at Chicago on 1835-07-01, and this edit moves no residence, no `present_on_scene_date` and no grade. The identity is the books crosswalk's landed merge (T-0961) and is not re-opened here.

reason_for_coming.value: A store for the traffic of a town filling up
reason_for_coming.note: ARGUED FROM THIS HOUSEHOLD'S OWN RECORDED TRADE, WHICH IS NOT ITS MOTIVE. The head is recorded as merchant, and this names the documented draw that trade answered in this town in this decade. It does not claim to know why these people came. Which of these draws brought this household is not recorded, and no committed source apportions the town between them.

basis.note: arrival_fill.trade_reasons.a_store_for_the_traffic — the head's recorded trade is evidence about this household, and the draw it answered is the reason the record will carry until a source states one.

replaceable_by.match: a source that says why this household came, or a committed source that apportions the town's arrivals between the land sales, the canal and the harbour works

lives_at.note: Andreas's residents list places 'James Kinzie and family' near Wentworth's tavern and this dataset's james_kinzie_house sits in that row, south of the tavern, on the strength of the same clause. Inferred rather than documented because the building record itself calls its evidence 'a single clause' and grades its own position inferred.

works_at.note: NOT ATTESTED AT THE SCENE DATE. He built the Green Tree and Chester Ingersoll kept it; he built a tavern on the west side of the South Branch and a Mr Crook kept it. This dataset holds james_kinzie_house as his residence and that is a lives_at, not a works_at.

present_on_scene_date.note: Continuous in the Chicago record across the period.

modelled_family.note: The kin core only. A servant, an apprentice or a journeyman this house may have held is priced by T-1183 and seated by T-1173; a boarder is seated by T-1175. The drawn size is a floor on the house.

kin.note: JAMES KINZIE IS THE HALF BROTHER OF JOHN HARRIS KINZIE, IN THE FORM THE SOURCE GIVES IT. Hurlbut's bracketed note under an American Fur Company outfit entry of 1821 reads '[The late James Kinzie, formerly of Chicago, and half brother of the late John H. Kinzie.]', filed as bk_afc_015 in data/research/books/claims/american_fur_company_hurlbut.json. HALF IS THE WHOLE POINT: the same father and different mothers, and it is the first thing a summary flattens. INFERRED RATHER THAN ATTESTED, AND THE GRADE IS WHAT AN 1881 EDITORIAL NOTE IS WORTH. This is not the town's contemporary paper but Hurlbut's own identification, printed sixty years after the consignment it annotates and after both men were dead, and this project reads it through Genealogy Trails' transcription rather than the original volume. It is a good source for the fact and it is still a recollection, so the relationship is reasoned from it rather than read off a record. A KINSHIP IS NOT A PLACEMENT. Nothing about either household's position, arrival, trade or membership rests on this row, and Hurlbut writing in 1881 about 1821 does not touch the scene date. What it does defend is the thing a shared surname keeps endangering: four household cards in this dataset are Kinzies — six until T-0839 folded two duplicate initials cards into their named men on 2026-09-05, which is the prior question T-0732 had to settle before it could rule on this family at all — data/research/books/crosswalk.json already has to refuse 'Mr. John Kinzie' the elder silversmith against John Harris Kinzie his son, and two men recorded as HALF brothers are two men, explicitly.

persons.name: James Kinzie

associated_with.note: GROUND HE BOUGHT, WHICH IS NOT GROUND HE STOOD ON — the rung is `tract` for that reason, and `land_purchased` is in neither the home kinds nor the work kinds because a holding is not a place a man was. The federal tract-sale register carries 1 row(s) — ls0053 — to this purchaser, read as 'KINZIE JAMES', sorted onto canal_section_9_remainder by tools/sort_land_sales_onto_tracts.py and covering about 80.0 acre(s) of it. THE TIER IS INFERRED AND THE TWO HALVES DIFFER: the purchase is documented — the register is a public record and states it — while the tie between that purchaser and THIS card is an identity ruling, upheld under T-0990 on 2026-09-11 by the rule 'KINZIE JAMES matches James Kinzie: the forename names James Kinzie of the 4 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full.'. The weaker half sets the tier. `to` is null because the register records a sale and not a tenure.

occupation.note: 'James Kinzie and family ... resided near Wentworth's tavern' in the list Andreas prints of the settlement's residents; he is a candidate at the 1833 town election and takes five votes. He built the Green Tree Tavern in 1833 and leased it, and he was surety on Mark Beaubien's ferry bond of 6 June 1831.

Kinzie.]” — the same father and different mothers, which is the form this dataset keeps, because flattening it to ‘brother’ is the move that lets the three Chicago Kinzies collapse into one another. Kinzie’ — is older than this reading, Hurlbut does not carry it, and it is neither cited nor upgraded here. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE.
